Our World: The week of Nov. 16, 2026
Our World is a roundup from our weekly print edition of noteworthy happenings, from our global correspondents and editors.
Ghana aims to boost domestic ore production
Ghana has set a target for banning unprocessed mineral exports, Bloomberg News reports. “By 2030, raw minerals should no longer leave our shores,” President John Mahama said recently during a mining conference in the capital, Accra. Africa’s biggest gold producer exports most of its precious metals unrefined, limiting how much it can profit from their sale. Mr. Mahama’s announcement comes as governments across the continent look to process more of their own ores domestically. Zimbabwe, Africa’s largest lithium producer, and the Democratic Republic of Congo, the world’s largest cobalt producer, have passed export bans over the years.  – Ryan Lenora Brown and Zachery Proctor    
Russia will harden data centers against drones
Vulnerable Russian data centers, whether state or private, will soon be expected to incorporate designs that withstand drone warfare, according to Russian news reports. After assessing the damage done by recent Ukrainian attacks on several data centers, Russia’s Digital Development Ministry has drawn up plans to ensure that most data facilities will be physically reinforced and armed for self-
defense, while those crucial to government function will be placed in bunkers. – Fred Weir    
“The world is not going to wait for us to get there.”
That’s what U.S. Sen. Dave McCormick, a Pennsylvania Republican, said during a recent visit to Hanwha Ocean’s main shipyard in Geoje, South Korea. The country’s large shipyards use robots and advanced engineering to crank out ships faster and cheaper than their competitors in the United States. Mr. McCormick’s trip, The Wall Street Journal reports, was part of a deepening industrial partnership between the U.S. and South Korea, with the latter promising to invest billions of dollars to revitalize American shipyards. South Korea has become the world’s second-largest source of commercial vessels, behind only China. Hanwha operates a plant in Philadelphia and is in talks to buy another shipyard in Alabama. – Lindsey McGinnis   
“It’s really important that we support our fantastic retail.”
That’s London Mayor Sadiq Khan, commenting on the pedestrianization of one of the busiest shopping streets in the world. More than half a mile of Oxford Street has been made traffic-free, with vehicles diverted onto nearby roads. Mr. Khan told ITV News it was a “momentous day” for London. But critics say the plan was rushed and have raised concerns about diverted traffic increasing congestion elsewhere.  – Tim Backshall
